name: decomposed-source-modules
body:
apg's first-party source must be well-decomposed, DRY, modular and maintainable: cohesive modules with a single clear responsibility, clear boundaries between them, and no duplicated logic. The goal is NOT to get files under a line count — line count is a signal, not a target. A large file is a prompt to inspect decomposition; a change that splits a file merely to hit a number, without improving cohesion, is itself a defect.

Scope: repo-wide over first-party source, excluding vendored code (`src/cpplib/vendor/**`) and testdata (`testdata/**`) — the root Rust crate (`src/*.rs` + `build.rs`) and the eight frontend crates (`structlib`, `pylib`, `rustlib`, `cpplib` non-vendor sources, `javalib`, `golib`, `csharplib`, `tslib`).

DRY is a first-class part of this requirement: shared logic must be single-sourced, never copy-pasted across modules. Concrete current instance (verified in the branch graph): scratch-repo test fixtures are duplicated across `mod tests` roots — `with_cwd` is defined four times (`rust.apg.tests.with_cwd` at `src/main.rs:2864`, `rust.apg.plan_cmd.tests.with_cwd` at `src/plan_cmd.rs:2469`, `rust.apg.node_cmd.tests.with_cwd` at `src/node_cmd.rs:512`, `rust.apg.review_cmd.tests.with_cwd` at `src/review_cmd.rs:1462`); `wt_commit` four times (`rust.apg.git.tests.wt_commit`, `rust.apg.node_cmd.tests.wt_commit`, `rust.apg.project_cmd.tests.wt_commit`, and the shared `rust.apg.testutil.wt_commit`); and `wt_commit_paths` twice (`rust.apg.artifacts.tests.wt_commit_paths`, `rust.apg.plan_cmd.tests.wt_commit_paths`). The shared harness `src/testutil.rs` already holds one copy of `wt_commit`, so the other copies are pure drift.

Acceptance criteria:
- No first-party production module is a grab-bag of unrelated responsibilities; each module's name and contents describe one concern.
- Shared logic has exactly one definition; a duplicated helper across modules is a defect.
- An over-large file is reviewed for decomposition, and any split is justified by improved cohesion — never by the line number alone.
- Completion is observable by review of the module set (names, responsibilities, and a duplicated-symbol inventory), not by a line-count threshold.
